content: The product contains a combination of monobasic sodium phosphate and dibasic sodium phosphate. It is indicated for use as a laxative to relieve occasional constipation and as part of a bowel cleansing regimen in preparation for colon surgery, x-ray imaging, or endoscopic examination. For administration, remove the orange protective shield from the enema tip before insertion. Gently insert the enema tip into the rectum with steady pressure, using a slight side-to-side motion, and ensure the tip is directed toward the navel. Insertion may be facilitated if the individual receiving the enema bears down as if having a bowel movement, which helps relax the anal muscles. Do not force the enema tip into the rectum, as this may cause injury. Squeeze the bottle until nearly all the liquid is expelled; it is not necessary to completely empty the bottle, as it contains more liquid than required. After removing the enema tip, the individual should maintain their position until the urge to evacuate becomes strong, typically within 1 to 5 minutes. The enema solution should not be retained for more than 10 minutes. Ensure the enema is at room temperature before use. For pediatric use: Do not use in children under 2 years of age. For children aged 2 to 4 years, administer half a bottle of the pediatric enema (~30 mL). Prepare the dose by unscrewing the cap, removing 2 tablespoons (30 mL) of liquid with a measuring spoon, replacing the cap, and administering the remaining liquid. For children aged 5 to 11 years, administer one full bottle of the pediatric enema (59 mL). For individuals aged 12 years or older, administer the adult enema as directed for adults. Sodium phosphate rectal preparations are contraindicated in certain conditions due to potential pharmacodynamic synergism, which may increase the effects or toxicity of other agents. Co-administration of various sodium phosphate preparations can lead to electrolyte disturbances and hypovolemia. Sodium phosphate rectal preparations may decrease the absorption or efficacy of certain medications, such as baloxavir marboxil, omadacycline, and sarecycline, due to cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. These interactions may impair drug absorption and reduce therapeutic efficacy. It is recommended to separate the dosing of tetracyclines and other affected medications from sodium phosphate products. Sodium phosphate rectal preparations may also decrease lithium levels by increasing renal clearance, particularly in cases of hypernatremia. Use caution or consider alternative therapies in such cases. Additionally, sodium phosphate rectal preparations and deflazacort may both decrease serum potassium levels, necessitating close monitoring. Adverse effects associated with sodium phosphate rectal preparations include hypersensitivity reactions, pruritus, dehydration, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypernatremia, metabolic acidosis, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, abdominal distension, diarrhea, gastrointestinal pain, chills, blistering, stinging, anal discomfort, and proctalgia. Severe dehydration and electrolyte abnormalities, such as hypernatremia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and hypokalemia, have been reported in cases of overdose or improper use, leading to complications such as acute kidney injury, arrhythmias, and even death. Use caution in patients with renal impairment, heart failure, electrolyte disturbances, or a history of seizures. Monitor closely in patients with comorbidities, elderly individuals, or children aged 2 to 11 years. Patients with pre-existing electrolyte imbalances or those taking diuretics or other medications that alter electrolytes should be monitored closely. Adequate hydration is essential to prevent dehydration and hypovolemia. Exceeding the recommended dose, retaining the enema solution for more than 10 minutes, or failure to have a bowel movement within 30 minutes of use may result in serious adverse effects. Sodium phosphate rectal preparations are contraindicated in conditions such as bowel obstruction, toxic megacolon, toxic colitis, gastric bypass or bariatric surgery, and in children under 5 years of age. They should not be used in the presence of nausea, vomiting, or severe abdominal pain. Caution is advised in patients with unstable angina, cardiomyopathy, prolonged QT interval, or a history of myocardial infarction. Preand post-dose ECGs and laboratory tests may be necessary in high-risk patients. Pregnancy Category C: The safety of sodium phosphate rectal preparations during pregnancy has not been established. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients should consult a healthcare professional before use due to the risk of electrolyte disturbances or dehydration.
